ANNOUNCING 
THE NEW 
 Y.M.C.A. CAMP 


ON 


ISLE PERROT 


28 MILES FROM MONTREAL

Girls - August 9th to August 23rd

INQUIRE AT YOUR . 
NEAREST Y.M:C: & 


LOCATION AND DESCRIPTION 


Camp Perrot is situated on the south shore of the Island 
of Perrot. It is a beautiful camp site overlooking the St. Law- 
rence River. The property is some forty-five acres in extent and 
has some six hundred feet of shore line. The swimming facilities 
are excellent and consist of a sandy, gradually sloping shore. 
There is a fine house, barn and summer cottage on the property, 
which will be used for various types of camp programs. The camp 
property lends itself to the development of an adequate games 
and waterfront program. 


There is a deep artesian well on the property which gives an 
ample supply of pure drinking water — tested. 


Campers will be housed in tents erected over wooden floors. 
Sleeping accommodation will consist of straw filled ticks. 


Plans are under way for the development of a vegetable and 
small fruit farm which will give those campers interested an 
opportunity to secure a real farm experience. 


The camp is located some six miles from St. Annes, on Isie 
Perrot. 


WHO MAY GO 


Any boy or girl 10 to 16 years of age. In order to allow a 
large number of children to attend, campers are restricted to a 
maximum of two weeks. 


CAMP STAFF 


The program for the Boys’ Camp will be in charge of the 
Boys’ Work Secretaries, and for the Girls’ Camp in charge of 
the Girls’ Work Secretaries. Mr. Beven Monks, a graduate in 
Agriculture from McDonald College, will be the Resident Mana- 
ger. Mrs. Monks, a registered nurse, will act as camp nurse. 
Food Service will be under the supervision of a competent chef. 


DATES FOR THE BOYS’ CAMP 


Wednesday, June 28th to Wednesday, August 9th. A boy 
may register for one or two weeks. The maximum stay is two 
weeks. Conducted parties leave and return from the camp on 
Wednesdays. 


DATES FOR GIRLS’ CAMP 


Wednesday, August 9th to Wednesday, August 23rd. 


TRANSPORTATION 


Campers will take the train to St. Annes, leaving from Windsor 
Station on Wednesdays at 12.15 noon. Campers will arrive back 
at the Windsor Station at 11.50 a.m. on Wednesdays. All parties 
are conducted from the station to the camp and return. From 
the St. Annes Station to the Camp is a distance of six miles. 
Luggage is taken by truck. 


COST 


Camp rates are seven dollars, $7.00 a week. Campers provide 
their own transportation. 


EQUIPMENT 


3 blankets, pillow, toilet articles, towels, bathing suit, soap, 
bible and clothes suitable for camp. 


N.B.—Each camper must supply eating utensils, i.e., plate, cup, 
bowl, knife, fork, large and small spoon. 


Bring ration book. 


VISITORS 


Parents may visit the camp on Sundays. 


WEEKEND CAMPERS 


Working Boys and Girls can make arrangements through 
the nearest Y.M.C.A. to go to the camp from Saturday afternoon 
to Sunday evening at a cost of $1.40 plus transportation.
